items.q: Grandma ______ the sticky rice for Tết right now, so the kitchen is full of steam.
items.vi: Bà đang đồ xôi cho Tết ngay lúc này nên bếp đầy hơi nước.
items.explanation:
Right now marks an action in progress at the moment of speaking, so the present continuous is steaming is needed.
✗ steams — present simple is for habits and routines, not what is happening now; ✗ has steamed — present perfect means the cooking is finished, but the kitchen is still full of steam; ✗ steamed — past simple puts the action in the past, clashing with right now.

items.q: Vegetables are cheap at the village market; a whole basket of tomatoes only ______ 20,000 dong.
items.vi: Rau ở chợ làng rất rẻ; cả một rổ cà chua chỉ có giá 20.000 đồng.
items.explanation:
Word choice: the subject is a thing (a basket of tomatoes) and the object is a sum of money, so the verb is costs = has a price of.
✗ pays — a person pays money; tomatoes cannot pay; ✗ spends — a person spends money on something; ✗ charges — a seller charges a customer a price; a basket cannot charge anyone.

items.q: Lan: The recipe says 200 grams of sugar, but you used 210. / Nam: Let's not ______ — ten grams won't change the taste.
items.vi: Lan: Công thức ghi 200 gam đường mà cậu cho 210. / Nam: Đừng bắt bẻ từng li từng tí — mười gam chẳng làm đổi vị đâu.
items.explanation:
Idiom: Nam refuses to argue over a tiny ten-gram difference, so split hairs = argue about small, unimportant details.
✗ pull strings — use influence to get a favour; ✗ cut corners — do a job cheaply or carelessly; ✗ beat around the bush — avoid saying the main point directly. None of these describes fussing over a small difference.

items.q: Could you ______ the table before the guests arrive for the New Year dinner?
items.vi: Con dọn bàn ăn trước khi khách đến dự bữa tối năm mới được không?
items.explanation:
Collocation: putting out plates and cutlery before the guests arrive is lay the table (also set the table).
✗ make — you make a bed or a cake, not a table for dinner; ✗ put — needs a place (put it on the table) and has no sense of preparing; ✗ do — 'do the table' is not an English expression for preparing it.

items.q: Our class won the school football final, ______ everyone because we had lost every practice match.
items.vi: Lớp mình đã thắng trận chung kết bóng đá của trường, điều đó làm mọi người bất ngờ vì bọn mình thua hết các trận giao hữu.
items.explanation:
Relative clause: after a comma, which can refer back to the whole previous clause (winning the final) — that is what surprised everyone.
✗ that surprised — that cannot begin a non-defining clause after a comma; ✗ what surprised — what = 'the thing that' and cannot add a comment to a clause; ✗ it surprised — starts a new independent clause, so a comma alone cannot join it (comma splice).

items.q: I can't ______ the barking from the neighbours' dogs any longer; it goes on all night.
items.vi: Tôi không thể chịu đựng tiếng sủa của mấy con chó nhà hàng xóm thêm nữa; nó kéo dài suốt đêm.
items.explanation:
Phrasal verb: the speaker can no longer tolerate the barking (can't … any longer), so put up with = accept something unpleasant without complaining.
✗ put off — postpone, or make someone dislike something; ✗ put out — extinguish a fire or light; ✗ put away — store something in its place. Only put up with takes 'the barking' as something to bear.

items.q: The restaurant added a ten per cent service ______ to our bill, so the meal cost more than we expected.
items.vi: Nhà hàng cộng thêm 10% phí phục vụ vào hóa đơn nên bữa ăn đắt hơn chúng tôi tưởng.
items.explanation:
Word choice: a percentage added to a bill for a service is a service charge; a charge is the amount a business asks for a service.
✗ price — what goods are sold for, not an extra added to a bill; ✗ fare — the money paid for a bus, taxi or train journey; ✗ cost — what something costs you overall; 'service cost' is not the fixed term.

items.q: By the time we reached the market, the fishmonger ______ every last prawn.
items.vi: Lúc chúng tôi tới chợ thì người bán cá đã bán hết sạch tôm.
items.explanation:
Tense: By the time we reached is a past point, and the selling was already complete before it, so the past perfect had sold is needed.
✗ has sold — present perfect links to now, not to a past moment; ✗ sold — past simple would make the selling happen at the same time as our arrival; ✗ was selling — past continuous means the sale was still going on, but every last prawn shows it was finished.

items.q: There's only ______ milk left in the fridge, so I can't make pancakes for everyone.
items.vi: Trong tủ lạnh chỉ còn một ít sữa nên mình không làm bánh kếp cho cả nhà được.
items.explanation:
Quantifier: milk is an uncountable noun, so it needs a little = a small amount.
✗ a few — used only with plural countable nouns (a few eggs); ✗ few — also plural countable, and means 'almost none'; ✗ many — plural countable, and 'many' contradicts only … left.

items.q: You ______ feed the goldfish more than once a day, or it will get sick.
items.vi: Con không được cho cá vàng ăn quá một lần mỗi ngày, nếu không nó sẽ bị bệnh.
items.explanation:
Modal: the warning or it will get sick shows that feeding more than once a day is forbidden, so mustn't = it is prohibited.
✗ needn't — means 'it is not necessary', not 'it is harmful'; ✗ don't have to — same as needn't, no prohibition; ✗ might not — expresses possibility ('perhaps you won't'), not a rule.

items.q: We ______ nearly all our pocket money on snacks at the Mid-Autumn fair.
items.vi: Chúng tôi tiêu gần hết tiền tiêu vặt vào đồ ăn vặt ở hội chợ Trung thu.
items.explanation:
Word choice: the object is money (pocket money) and the pattern is spend money on something, so spent is correct.
✗ paid — you pay a person or pay for something; 'pay money on' is wrong; ✗ bought — you buy goods, not money; ✗ cost — things cost money; people are not the subject of cost.

items.q: Lan: Your parrot can say a few words, ______? / Nam: Yes, it says 'hello' every morning.
items.vi: Lan: Con vẹt của cậu nói được vài từ, phải không? / Nam: Ừ, sáng nào nó cũng nói 'hello'.
items.explanation:
Question tag: a positive statement takes a negative tag with the same auxiliary. The verb here is the modal can, so the tag is can't it.
✗ can it — a positive tag after a positive statement; ✗ isn't it — repeats be, but the sentence has no is; ✗ doesn't it — do is used only when there is no auxiliary, and here can is the auxiliary.

items.q: The vet told us to ______ the puppy a bath every two weeks, not every day.
items.vi: Bác sĩ thú y dặn chúng tôi tắm cho chó con hai tuần một lần, chứ không phải mỗi ngày.
items.explanation:
Collocation: when you wash a pet or a child, you give it a bath; the bath is something done to the puppy.
✗ take — you take (or have) a bath yourself; you cannot 'take someone a bath'; ✗ make — 'make a bath' is not a collocation; ✗ do — 'do a bath' does not exist in English.

items.q: If it ______ so heavily, the village wouldn't have called off the boat race.
items.vi: Nếu trời không mưa to như vậy thì làng đã không hủy cuộc đua thuyền.
items.explanation:
Third conditional: the main clause wouldn't have called off (would have + past participle) shows an unreal past, so the if-clause needs the past perfect hadn't rained.
✗ didn't rain — past simple builds a second conditional (would + verb) about the present; ✗ wouldn't rain — would belongs in the main clause, not after if; ✗ doesn't rain — present simple makes a first conditional about a real future.

items.q: The soup smelt wonderful; ______, it was far too salty to eat.
items.vi: Món canh thơm tuyệt; tuy nhiên, nó mặn quá không ăn nổi.
items.explanation:
Linking word: the soup smelt wonderful but was too salty — two opposite ideas — so however is needed.
✗ therefore — introduces a result, but being salty is not caused by smelling good; ✗ moreover — adds a similar point, not an opposite one; ✗ because — gives a reason, and a conjunction cannot sit between a semicolon and a comma like this.

items.q: The pet shop gave us a small ______ because the cage had a scratch on one side.
items.vi: Cửa hàng thú cưng giảm giá một chút cho chúng tôi vì cái lồng bị xước một bên.
items.explanation:
Word choice: money taken off the price because the cage had a scratch is a discount.
✗ bargain — something bought at a good price, not the amount taken off; a shop does not 'give a bargain'; ✗ sale — a period when a shop lowers all its prices; ✗ bonus — extra money paid to a worker or an added benefit, not a price cut.

items.q: Don't forget ______ the hamster's cage before we leave for the festival.
items.vi: Đừng quên dọn lồng chuột hamster trước khi chúng ta đi lễ hội nhé.
items.explanation:
Gerund vs infinitive: forget + to-infinitive = forget a task you still need to do. The cage has not been cleaned yet (before we leave), so to clean is right.
✗ cleaning — forget doing = have no memory of something already done; ✗ clean — a bare infinitive cannot follow forget; ✗ to cleaning — to + -ing is not a form forget takes.

items.q: It took Mai several weeks to ______ the loss of her old cat.
items.vi: Mai phải mất mấy tuần mới nguôi ngoai nỗi mất con mèo già của mình.
items.explanation:
Phrasal verb: recovering from a sad experience (the loss of her old cat) is get over = recover from.
✗ get by — manage to live with little money; ✗ get along — have a friendly relationship with someone; ✗ get up — rise from bed. Only get over takes 'the loss' as its object.

items.q: Neither the dog nor the cats ______ allowed in the kitchen while Mum is cooking.
items.vi: Cả con chó lẫn mấy con mèo đều không được vào bếp khi mẹ đang nấu ăn.
items.explanation:
Agreement: with neither … nor the verb agrees with the nearer subject, the cats (plural), and while Mum is cooking keeps it in the present, so are.
✗ is — singular, would agree with the far subject the dog; ✗ was — singular and past, but the rule is present; ✗ has been — singular present perfect; neither the number nor the tense fits.

items.q: You should ______ if the butcher tries to charge more than the price on the sign.
items.vi: Bạn nên giữ vững lập trường nếu người bán thịt cố tính giá cao hơn giá ghi trên bảng.
items.explanation:
Idiom: refusing to accept a price higher than the price on the sign is stand your ground = refuse to give in.
✗ hold your tongue — stay silent, the opposite of arguing back; ✗ pull your weight — do your fair share of the work; ✗ mind your step — be careful where you walk. Only stand your ground fits a price dispute.

items.q: My uncle ______ dogs since he was a little boy, and he still has three.
items.vi: Chú tôi nuôi chó từ hồi còn bé, và giờ chú vẫn nuôi ba con.
items.explanation:
Tense: since he was a little boy gives a starting point and he still has three shows the situation continues to now, so the present perfect has kept is needed.
✗ keeps — present simple cannot combine with since + past time; ✗ kept — past simple would mean he stopped keeping dogs; ✗ is keeping — present continuous describes only now, not a period from the past.

items.q: ______ the mooncakes, Mai carried a plate of them next door for the neighbours.
items.vi: Nướng xong bánh trung thu, Mai bưng một đĩa sang nhà hàng xóm.
items.explanation:
Participle clause: Mai finished baking before carrying the plate, so the perfect participle Having baked shows the earlier, completed action.
✗ Baking — present participle means both actions happen at the same time; she cannot carry a plate of finished cakes while still baking them; ✗ Baked — past participle is passive and would make Mai the thing that was baked; ✗ To bake — an infinitive of purpose ('in order to bake') makes no sense here.

items.q: The two puppies love chasing ______ around the garden all afternoon.
items.vi: Hai chú chó con thích rượt đuổi nhau quanh vườn suốt buổi chiều.
items.explanation:
Pronoun: the two puppies chase one another — an action going both ways — so the reciprocal pronoun each other is needed.
✗ themselves — reflexive: each puppy would be chasing its own self; ✗ itself — singular reflexive, but the subject is plural; ✗ another — means 'a different one', and there is no third puppy.

items.q: My aunt ______ about 500,000 dong a month by selling homemade fish sauce online.
items.vi: Dì tôi kiếm được khoảng 500.000 đồng một tháng nhờ bán nước mắm nhà làm trên mạng.
items.explanation:
Word choice: getting money by working or selling is earn, so earns about 500,000 dong a month.
✗ wins — you win a prize, a race or a game, not a monthly income; ✗ gains — you gain weight, experience or confidence, not a sum of money from work; ✗ charges — a seller charges a customer a price for an item, not 'charges 500,000 dong a month'.

items.q: The whole village ______ part in the lantern parade every autumn.
items.vi: Cả làng đều tham gia rước đèn mỗi mùa thu.
items.explanation:
Collocation: the fixed expression for joining an activity is take part in, so the village takes part in the parade.
✗ makes — 'make part in' is not an expression; ✗ does — 'do part in' does not exist; ✗ gets — 'get part in' is wrong; you can only 'get a part' in a play, which is a role, a different meaning.
